title: Cadenza Health — VPC / private deploy scoping & ops scratchbook
content:
Context / why this doc exists:
- Quick personal capture from scoping calls with Cadenza Health (CH). They are evaluating a VPC-hosted private deployment (no hosted API) — primary drivers: PHI handling, on-prem-like networking controls, KMS integration, and strict audit logs.
- Goal: capture requirements, gotchas we surfaced, capacity estimates, and a minimal path to POC.

Last sync (2025-11-01) — attendees:
- CH: Emily Park (CTO), Sanjay Rao (Infra lead), Lina Gomez (Security)
- Redwood: Maya (SE), Ravi (private deploy eng), Sophie (security).

High-level ask (from Emily):
- Full VPC-based control plane (customer-managed VPC peering or private link).
- On-prem gateway / air-gap option for model artifacts during onboarding.
- HSM/KMS integration (Azure Key Vault + on-prem HSM preferred).
- SLA-like objective on 99.9% availability for inference with p50 latency < 120ms for 512-token responses.

Requirements we captured (rough):
- Network:
  * Outbound-only control-plane callbacks blocked by default; customer wants explicit egress allowlist.
  * Ports: 443 for control plane; 22 only for console-managed debug windows (needs approval flow).
  * VPC peering preferred; Transit Gateway as fallback. Must support cross-account routing.
- Security:
  * KMS integration via customer-managed keys; HSM wrap support.
  * Audit logs forwarded to Splunk/Elastic — 365 day retention (CH security mandate).
  * RBAC via SSO (SAML Okta); token expiry policies configurable.
  * Data-at-rest: prefer model weights encrypted with CMK and disk-level encryption.
- Compliance:
  * PHI controls: disable prompt/response retention by default, optional short-term buffers that must be explicitly approved.
  * e2e TLS for all internal links and client-facing endpoints.
- Operational:
  * Canary rollout for model version changes (gradual ramp 1% -> 50% -> 100%), with automatic rollback on error rate > 2% or latency regression > 30%.
  * Observability: token-level latency, per-request trace ids, per-model cost estimate.
- Capacity / perf:
  * Expected steady-state: 12 concurrent QPS average, spikes to 120 QPS for 30m windows (health checks / batch jobs).
  * Target per-token cost sensitivity: they want unit economics similar to hosted offering within 15% premium.

Initial sizing note (ballpark) — dependent on model family:
- Small-medium models (7B quantized): 2x A10G nodes (4 GPUs) with batching -> target p50 ~ 80–120ms for 512 tokens.
- Large models (30–70B): horizontal pool of 4–6 H100-style nodes; expect higher per-token cost, need caching to be effective.
- Recommendation: start POC on 7B quantized variant to validate latency & routing, then benchmark 30B if acceptance criteria met.

Gotchas / things to watch (pain notes):
- MTU and overlay networks: CH uses 9000 MTU across their datacenter; our default images sometimes assume 1500 and some GPU drivers + RDMA stacks can break if mismatch. Need to validate early.
- NAT / ephemeral IPs: ephemeral egress in their VPC is proxied through a NAT instance; control-plane callback retries may be delayed — add jitter/backoff tuning.
- KMS & cold-start timing: if each model shard requires CMK unwrap on load, cold starts can balloon. Explore key caching or envelope-key patterns.
- Model cache warmup: Their workload is bursty; ensure prefix caching and warmup scripts are part of deploy playbook.
- Telemetry noise: Splunk ingest costs — our audit logs can be noisy at token-level. Offer a summarized log mode as a compromise.

Open technical questions (to resolve before POC):
1) Is CH okay with outbound-only control plane (we need at least an initial outbound control channel for infra healthchecks)? Lina to confirm.
2) HSM vendor + integration specifics: is their HSM reachable via VPC endpoints or do we need on-prem connector? Sanjay to share vendor docs.
3) Do they require private model artifact storage (S3 gateway) in their account or will Redwood-hosted artifact store behind VPC work during onboarding?
4) What exact SLOs are contract-worthy vs. POC?: 99.9% vs 99.5% — Emily to align with procurement.

Immediate next steps / action items:
- (Maya) Draft a POC runbook that includes: VPC peering steps, required IAM perms, quick MTU sanity checks, and an ops debug checklist. Due 2025-11-07.
- (Ravi) Prototype KMS envelope-key caching in a small test harness and measure cold-start time difference. Due 2025-11-14.
- (Sophie) Sketch audit log sampling options (full, sampled, summarized) with Splunk cost impact estimates. Due 2025-11-10.
- (CH - Sanjay) Share HSM vendor docs and network topology diagram (including NAT behavior) by 2025-11-05.
- (Maya + Emily) Run a short latency bench using internal 7B quantized model on 2025-11-12 (tentative).

POC acceptance criteria (proposal):
- p50 latency <= 120ms for 512 tokens under steady 12 QPS traffic for 30 minutes.
- Can handle a spike to 120 QPS for at least 15 minutes with degraded but functional responses (p95 <= 2s).
- KMS integration validated: keys used for model artifact encryption and unwrap time < 500ms per node when cached.
- Security checklist completed: Okta SAML test, audit forwarding established, no unapproved egress rules.

Quick runbook excerpt (commands / examples):
- Boot node with VPC endpoint: (placeholder) -> ensure security group egress only to control plane IPs.
- cURL (control-plane handshake test):
  curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" https://controlplane.example.internal/healthz

Notes to self (loose):
- Keep this doc messy — action items/priorities will migrate to a Confluence playbook once CH signs an NDA.
- Avoid promising timelines for model-size benchmarking until we validate MTU and KMS warmup.
- Consider a hybrid approach: start with Redwood-managed artifact store but run EDH (envelope data handling) so CH can move to fully customer-managed storage later.

Reference links we discussed:
- Confluence baseline template (internal): PD/VPC-DEPLOY-TEMPLATES
- Jira ticket capturing procurement ask: PD-1243
- Internal PR for private-deploy bootstrap: github.com/redwood-inference/private-deploy/pull/345

End of scratchbook capture — will tidy into a formal POC runbook after CH confirms HSM networking and egress policy.
